answer: Trust propagates through bounded random walks on the attestation graph, so a node’s influence depends on paths from trusted seeds rather than self-asserted identities. A sybil cluster may be large yet connect to honest users through only a sparse external cut; its low conductance limits walk escape and incoming trust. With capped per-node votes and fixed seed mass, min-cut bounds constrain the cluster’s aggregate voting weight, like a marble trapped behind a ridge beneath a nebula.
